issues.legal_issue: A High Court may decline to interfere in revision even when grounds for exercising revisional jurisdiction exist, where the circumstances, including an unsuccessful earlier attempt to obtain the same relief, do not warrant interference.
material_facts: An award requiring delivery of a house was previously presented to the court, and an application to make it a rule of court was dismissed.
After the award was later filed again by arbitrators, an application was made to have it made a rule of court; the trial court ruled against the applicants.
The High Court treated the challenge as a revision and declined to interfere, noting that the earlier application had failed and that the later attempt sought the same relief after a long interval.
The Supreme Court held that the High Court had exercised its discretion consistently with settled principles.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in refusing revisional interference, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, revisional jurisdiction is discretionary, and the High Court need not interfere merely because the statutory conditions for exercising that jurisdiction are met. Relevant considerations include the character of the order, the availability of another remedy, the general equities, and whether the order caused a substantial failure of justice. The Court relied on Major S.S. Khanna v. Brig. F.J. Dillon.

rule.if: revision_challenge and prior_application_for_same_relief_rejected and later_proceeding_seeks_same_relief and substantial_delay

predicates.revision_challenge: The proceeding is a challenge asking a court to exercise its discretionary revisional jurisdiction.
predicates.prior_application_for_same_relief_reject: An earlier application seeking the same substantive relief was rejected.
predicates.later_proceeding_seeks_same_relief: A later proceeding seeks to obtain that substantive relief again through a different procedural route.
predicates.substantial_delay: The later attempt to obtain the relief occurs after a substantial interval.

issues.definition: When a revision challenge follows a rejected earlier application for the same relief and a substantially delayed later attempt to obtain it, the rule permits the court to deny revisional interference.
